title: Staged and partial transaction semantics
requirement: When a supported transaction spans several settlement steps, Moriarty shall represent each committed step and the outstanding transaction state explicitly.
motivation: A local transaction succeeds while a later receipt or withdrawal fails.
theory_directions: Trace semantics, small-step operational semantics, refinement of distributed histories
positive_scenario: Prove each accepted prefix preserves authority, accounting and outstanding duties; do not label a successful prefix complete.
negative_scenario: An accepted debit followed by an unresolved withdrawal is reported as fully settled.

title: Typed persistent continuations
requirement: When execution suspends for a later event, Moriarty shall persist a typed continuation bound to the program, predecessor, awaited events, authority and outstanding duties.
motivation: NEAR promises and callbacks resume across transactions without a fresh original-user signature.
theory_directions: Session types, typestate, affine capabilities, defunctionalization, continuation typing
positive_scenario: Resume a valid continuation once with correctly typed evidence and the signed stage policy.
negative_scenario: Replay or attach an unrelated callback to consume reserved authority twice.

title: Conditional settlement with composable evidence
requirement: When a submitted transaction specifies settlement conditions, Moriarty shall withhold the specified delivery until the required combination of authenticated signatures, documentary evidence, proofs, recipient actions and other supported predicates is satisfied.
motivation: User definition: submit to an address; settlement waits for the configured combination of conditions. Funding or recording may precede final delivery.
theory_directions: Refinement/dependent types, proof-relevant predicates, evidence algebra, authorization logic
positive_scenario: A funded request remains pending until its bound recipient signature, document predicate and proof all validate at the policy-defined settlement point.
negative_scenario: A document hash alone, an unrelated signature, or an expired proof releases the funds.

title: Partial fulfillment and residual duties
requirement: When a signed policy permits partial fulfillment, each accepted fill shall satisfy its fill rules and preserve cumulative bounds, remaining authority and residual obligations.
motivation: A completed portion of a swap or payment is not the entire economic obligation.
theory_directions: Linear logic, resource algebras, quantitative types, financial contract semantics
positive_scenario: Two valid partial payments reduce the liability by exactly their authorized discharges.
negative_scenario: Splitting a fill bypasses a cumulative fee bound or erases remaining debt.

title: Refunds and compensation
requirement: When a settlement step fails or remains unresolved, recovery shall distinguish a refund of still-controlled assets from a new compensating action after effects have committed.
motivation: A failed downstream promise may not imply that transferred value is available for refund.
theory_directions: Sagas, compensating calculi, exception/effect semantics, recovery invariants
positive_scenario: A recovery transition spends only assets or claims it actually controls and retains unrecovered duties.
negative_scenario: Compensation rewrites history or issues a second refund after external delivery.

title: Authenticated asynchronous outcomes
requirement: When evidence resumes a stage, Moriarty shall authenticate its origin, correlation and declared finality, and enforce the specified consumption rule.
motivation: Receipt IDs, returned values and detached calls have different authority and completion meaning.
theory_directions: Affine evidence tokens, capability security, event provenance, replay-safe protocols
positive_scenario: A duplicated delivery is harmless or rejected without duplicate financial effects.
negative_scenario: An attacker substitutes a success flag or callback from another transaction.

title: Joins and late results
requirement: When a program joins asynchronous branches, it shall specify availability and success policies separately and retain duties for unselected or late branches.
motivation: A NEAR join can make failed results available; readiness does not imply all-success.
theory_directions: Session types, choreographies, concurrent separation logic, join patterns
positive_scenario: A quorum branch proceeds under its signed rule while late branches remain accounted for.
negative_scenario: An any-success join drops the debit or refund duty of a losing branch.

title: Stage-specific authority and consent
requirement: When a stage executes, it shall use only the authority and consent granted for that stage under the signed lifecycle, revocation and expiry policy.
motivation: Callbacks do not freshly consume the originating access-key nonce; delegated workflow authority must be explicit.
theory_directions: Authorization logic, capability attenuation, session fidelity, temporal capabilities
positive_scenario: Recipient consent is bound to the exact request, amount, asset, conditions and allowed amendment version.
negative_scenario: A callback gains the full original signer authority or changes the recipient silently.

title: Cumulative work fees and reserves
requirement: When execution spans stages, Moriarty shall account for cumulative costs, reserved resources and permitted retained fees under the signed bounds and target phase rules.
motivation: Receipt execution and failure can retain fees, rewards or storage consequences.
theory_directions: Amortized resource analysis, graded effects, quantitative type theory
language_comparisons: AARA languages, Resource Aware ML, Move
positive_scenario: A failed stage records retained fees and remaining reserves without exceeding its approved envelope.
negative_scenario: Retrying or splitting stages resets the total budget.

title: Time finality and unresolved outcomes
requirement: When a deadline or observation boundary is reached, Moriarty shall classify what is known and apply the signed expiry policy without treating missing evidence as proof of nonexecution.
motivation: Timeout, receipt failure, source finality and destination settlement are different facts.
theory_directions: Temporal logic, epistemic logic, distributed failure detectors, timed session types
positive_scenario: An expired request retains unresolved external duties until reliable evidence establishes the relevant delivery, cancellation, nonexecution or recovery outcome; any other residual duties remain.
negative_scenario: A late successful transfer is followed by a refund justified only by timeout.

title: Causality concurrency and interference
requirement: When a suspended workflow resumes amid other activity, its proof shall preserve predecessor causality and revalidate the relevant state and authority under its signed policy.
motivation: Other calls may change balances, keys, policy or custody between asynchronous stages.
theory_directions: Rely-guarantee reasoning, separation logic, serializability, conflict-aware refinement
positive_scenario: Concurrent valid workflows cannot consume the same reserve or invalidate each other silently.
negative_scenario: A simulation snapshot is reused after its relevant balance or authority changed.

title: Simulation and assurance status
requirement: When a tool simulates or reports a workflow, it shall state which stages, calls and proof judgments were covered and keep prediction separate from accepted execution.
motivation: Simulation may skip downstream AuthCall/withdrawal effects or return only a local engine result.
theory_directions: Abstract interpretation, trace refinement, effect summaries, proof-producing analysis
positive_scenario: A local preview visibly reports unresolved external stages and does not claim settlement.
negative_scenario: An omitted external call is displayed as successfully executed or proved.

title: Private evidence and continuations
requirement: Where evidence or workflow state is private, Moriarty shall define what each participant can observe and how later authorized stages obtain the witness needed to continue.
motivation: Documents, signatures, receipt correlations and multi-party continuation state may reveal sensitive facts.
theory_directions: Information-flow control, noninterference, zero-knowledge relations, secure session types
positive_scenario: Prove a required document property without disclosing fields outside the authorized view.
negative_scenario: A public status or continuation identifier leaks a property claimed confidential.

title: Certified lowering of staged effects
requirement: When a staged program is compiled, correspondence shall preserve its permitted traces, conditions, rejection behavior and costs in the pinned Midnight ZKIRv3 execution model.
motivation: NEAR receipt semantics cannot be assumed to match Midnight guaranteed/fallible phases.
theory_directions: Compiler correctness, observational refinement, certified primitives, effect preservation
positive_scenario: A target trace is related to a permitted source trace with every retained effect accounted for.
negative_scenario: A correct witness generator is presented as proof excluding invalid satisfying witnesses.

title: Open programmable financial workflows
requirement: When a developer composes supported constructs into a new workflow, validation shall use the versioned language and proof rules rather than a catalog of approved example programs.
motivation: A fixed Intents enum is a useful application protocol but not the identity of a general DeFi language.
theory_directions: Algebraic effects, extensible DSLs, modular semantics, refinement interfaces
positive_scenario: A newly authored conditional workflow passes the ordinary public pipeline.
negative_scenario: A valid program is rejected because it is absent from a project registry.

title: Application authority versus project access
requirement: When an application restricts participants or evidence issuers, Moriarty shall enforce its authenticated policy without imposing project approval on public program deployment.
motivation: Hosted relay screening, contract admin roles and owner authorization operate at different boundaries.
theory_directions: Capability security, authorization logic, module boundaries, policy refinement
positive_scenario: A user can require a particular counterparty signature while independent developers deploy supported programs freely.
negative_scenario: A hosted service credential or reviewer receipt becomes mandatory proof evidence.

title: Complete staged financial accounting
requirement: When a stage is accepted, its authenticated effect frame shall account for exact assets and custody, authorized supply changes, fees and separately typed liability evolution.
motivation: Internal token-delta balance, external custody and residual economic duties are not interchangeable quantities.
theory_directions: Resource separation algebras, nominal asset types, linear accounting, invariant composition
positive_scenario: Every asset transfer and liability change has its own well-typed conservation/evolution equation.
negative_scenario: Authority units are added to refund amounts, or internal zero-sum balance is called external settlement.

title: Inspectable conditional intent
requirement: When a participant authorizes a conditional workflow, the signing and reporting interface shall expose its canonical conditions, destination, evidence policy, allowed partial outcomes and recovery rules.
motivation: A quote, signature request or pending status can hide distinctions important to the user’s actual intention.
theory_directions: Bidirectional transformations, contract elaboration, semantic UI correspondence, typed provenance
positive_scenario: The displayed request and proved canonical object bind the same documents, recipient consent, deadline and remedies.
negative_scenario: The UI promises automatic refund while the signed policy permits an unresolved or compensating outcome.
